Germanic cognates include Old High German thurst, Middle High German durst, German Durst, Old Saxon thurst, Old Dutch thursti, Middle Dutch dorst, dorste, Dutch dorst, Old Norse þorsti (Swedish törst, Icelandic þorsti, Faroese tosti, Danish and Norwegian Bokmål tørst, Norwegian Nynorsk tørste). Indo-European cognates include Ancient Greek τέρσομαι (térsomai), Albanian djersë (“sweat”), Sanskrit तृष्णा (tṛṣṇā, “desire; thirst”), Sanskrit तृष्यति (tṛ́ṣyati), Latin terra, Latin torridus.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English we, from Old English wē (“we”), from Proto-West Germanic *wiʀ, from Proto-Germanic *wīz, *wiz (“we”), from Proto-Indo-European *wéy (“we (plural)”). Cognate with Scots wee, we (“we”), North Frisian we (“we”), West Frisian wy (“we”), Low German wi (“we”), Dutch we, wij (“we”), German wir (“we”), Danish, Swedish and Norwegian vi (“we”), Icelandic vér, við (“we”), Avestan 𐬬𐬀𐬉𐬨 (vaēm), Sanskrit वयम् (vayám).

senses.definition: Used by a speaker to refer to themselves and one or more other people.

examples.en: We are going to the park this afternoon.
examples.vi: Chiều nay chúng tôi sẽ đi công viên.

examples.en: We should help each other.
examples.vi: Chúng ta nên giúp đỡ lẫn nhau.

senses.definition: Used to refer to people in general, including the speaker.

examples.en: We often learn more from failure than success.
examples.vi: Chúng ta thường học hỏi được nhiều điều từ thất bại hơn là thành công.

senses.definition: Used in instructions or explanations to involve the listener or reader.

examples.en: Next, we add a cup of water to the pot.
examples.vi: Tiếp theo, chúng ta cho một cốc nước vào nồi.

senses.definition: Used instead of 'you' when speaking to someone you are caring for.

examples.en: How are we feeling after taking the medicine?
examples.vi: Sau khi uống thuốc xong thì mình cảm thấy thế nào rồi?

examples: We are here to arrest you.
wiktionary.gloss: Excluding the person(s) being addressed. (This is the exclusive we.)

examples: We need to have a talk, you and me.
wiktionary.gloss: Including the person(s) being addressed. (This is the inclusive we.)

examples: We will in due course state our reasons for publishing the name of the accused.
As the government, we have a duty to ensure public safety.
wiktionary.gloss: The institution which the speaker/writer is acting for. (This is the editorial we, used by writers and others when speaking with the authority of their publication or organisation.)

examples: I went to watch our school football match against Puddletown High. We lost 2-0.
In English, we do not inflect adjectives for gender.
wiktionary.gloss: Any other entity that the speaker is a part of or identifies with, such as place of employment or education, nation, region, language, etc.

examples: We live and learn.
We still have much to learn about quantum mechanics.
wiktionary.gloss: People in general.

examples: We are Queen of all these Isles.
wiktionary.gloss: The sovereign alone in his or her capacity as monarch. (This is the royal we. The reflexive case of this sense of we is ourself.)

examples: Good evening everyone. How are we all tonight?
wiktionary.gloss: Everyone being addressed.

examples: Hello Mrs Miggins. How are we feeling this morning?
You've been spending all your money boozing when you have a wife and family to support. I think we need to get our priorities straight.
wiktionary.gloss: An individual being addressed; used especially to a person in the speaker's care, or to whom advice or instruction is being given. (Sometimes called the nurse's we or the doctor's we.)

examples: "I've just been to see Mrs Miggins." — "And how is she?" — "I'm afraid we aren't too good today."
wiktionary.gloss: Used to refer to a third person, especially someone in the speaker's care.

examples: Hey guys, in this video I'll show you how I make my upside-down sponge cake. First we take 200 g of butter and we whisk in 200 g of sugar. Next, we ...
wiktionary.gloss: Used to imply connection between the speaker's experiences or activities and a group of listeners. (Compare the plural of modesty.)

examples: To solve the equation, we first collect all the terms in x on one side.
wiktionary.gloss: Used in explanatory or procedural writing, such as mathematical explanations, to imply inclusion of the reader in the undertaking.

examples: Now then ... let me see ... I hope I'm doing this right ... if we just connect these two wires together ...
wiktionary.gloss: Used when talking to oneself to refer to oneself.
The side which is keeping score.

examples: He was a propa gadgie, and always bought we drinks after a long shift.
